summary: The mechanism is real and already demonstrated end-to-end by the sibling check dfee6f2939974bad on muse_attention_decode (same four launches plus FusedQKNorm fused into one Triton kernel, 16/16 tests, fused kernel 1.3-1.5 us, 3.5-6.4 us saved per shape). Nothing landed interacts with the pre-attention stage, so one run is interpretable without companions; the expected decode_1 gain is ~2%, not 4-5%, which sits at the churn's 1.5% per-shape noise threshold and must be read from the per-shape rows against the merged base, not from the overall CI.
justification: Master (muse_decode_layer/submission.py:298-311) runs k.to(FP8), v.to(FP8), store_cache and q.to(FP8) serially on the main stream before FA3. Removing 3 of those 4 launches shortens the critical path on every shape. Sibling evidence (muse_attention_decode/profiles/submission.dfee6f2939974bad.txt): the 5->1 fusion saved 3.5-6.4 us per shape, ~1.0-1.6 us per removed launch under graph replay. Scaling to 3 removed: ~3-4.5 us against the merged base rows (decode_1 sliding 168.73 us, full 180.65; verify_1 sliding 233.99, full 250.89), i.e. ~1.8-2.0% on decode_1 and ~1.5-2.0% on verify_1; T>=16 shapes move <1%, correctly flat. Overall geomean moves ~+0.6%, inside the CI, so the signal lives in per-shape medians (err_ns at T=1 ~0.37%). Weakest link: the hypothesis's own numbers are inflated; the expected ~2% per-shape gain is only marginally above the 1.5% attribution noise, and the parity run showed a ~1% unexplained per-run offset at T=1. A true gain may be scored neutral by threshold; a flat result would not refute the mechanism.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (only landed item): changes ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS 8->1 on the side-stream router after the o projection; shares no launch, memory traffic or numerical path with the pre-attention cast/store stage. Additive, not interacting; its parity port fixes the base rows this run must be compared against.
interference: No companion. ab-revert of the router constant only perturbs T=8 rows via an unrelated path; nothing to re-tune; a control splitting the q-cast from the k/v cast+store is unnecessary since the sibling kernel already shows all pieces fused correctly, and any implementation loss is visible as extra or long kernels in the run's own profile. What the run needs is a reading rule: judge per shape against the merged base rows with err_ns.
rules_flags: Allocate the fp8 q buffer with torch.empty((T,16,64)) inside kernel_fn each call; do not stash a per-shape buffer in state.
No triton.autotune; fixed num_warps/BLOCK sizes chosen from config on the host.
kv_scale path: a Triton fp32 divide-then-cast is more precise than master's bf16 divide and matches the reference's _quant; allowed, only exercised by the kv_scale=1/64 test.
FP8 overflow semantics (NaN vs satfinite clamp) differ only where the reference itself would be NaN; no rule issue.
reserved_skip_index=-1 relies on cache_loc always valid; the kernel must not mask or branch on values.
Nothing derived from data is cached, no host syncs, FA3 call and window unchanged, q rounded to FP8 E4M3 as master already does; Triton JIT compiles on warm-up before capture.
open_questions: Expected decode_1 is ~1.8-2.0% (3-4 us), not 4-5%; treat a 2-4 us per-shape delta on the four T<=8 rows as success, against the merged base rows with err_ns.
store_cache is already a single kernel, so the saving is 3 launches.
A follow-up should port the sibling's _pre_attention_kernel (FusedQKNorm fused too) onto this base for a further ~1-1.5 us per shape.
Verify no at::native copy/elementwise kernel remains between FusedQKNorm and FA3 in the profile.
Confirm the fp8 q buffer handed to FA3 is [T,16,64] with unit last-dim stride and FA3 inserts no extra cast/copy.
